newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady, forwards biddish.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady, forwards biddish.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar and forward rates were well bid in slow early trading on Thursday, dealers said.
But the underlying tone for the dollar was biddish on the back of a relatively ample money market, with overnight money trading at around 8.5 percent in the morning.
"People were buying the rupiah on Wednesday on expectation of a tight market. But an ample turnout this morning caused operators to buy back some dollars," one U.S. bank dealer said.
He said, however, some built-in premiums for the weekend also weakened the rupiah from Wednesday's level.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.00/29.25 at 0300 GMT against an opening of 2,429.0/30.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,428.85/29.20 and 2,428.5/29.0, respectively.
"It's not that exiting to short dollars for now because of a sustained flush rupiah market. Some players are seen covering back apart from the weekend factor," the U.S. bank dealer said.
He said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,428.0 and 2,430 levels for the rest of the day.
Dealers said the Thai problem continued to hang over the Jakarta forward market, driving longer-term forward rates to increase each time offshore players were squeezed over there.
The Thai central bank had asked operators to stop quoting tom/next to offshore players to close their funding sources.
"Our forward market is a bit in disorder because of the Thai factor. Offshore players fear a similar move in Jakarta despite a denial by Bank Indonesia," another bank dealer said.
She said offshore players were going long in forwards to factor in possible risks although they have to pay for it.
"They keep buying three- and six-month swaps," she said.
"There is still some buying interest in the swap market. But cheap day-to-day roll over costs limit a further uptrend in the longer-end market," the U.S. bank dealer said.
Overnight swap was at 0.15/0.20 and tom/next at 0.10/0.15.
One-month swaps were at 11.5/12.5, two at 24.0/27.0, three at 37.0/39.0 and six at 76.0/78.0 points.
The central bank kpet its intervention band at 2,418/2,610 and its conversion band at 2,418/2,466 on Wednesday.
Dealers said last week's general election remained an issue because of complaints over irregularities.
But they said there was no doubt the ruling Golkar party had won the election despite vote-rigging complaints. Golkar took over 74 percent of the national vote.

Another impending issue was whether the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) would accept the election outcome. PPP leaders were meeting on Thursday and said they would make a statement on Friday.
